checks: Retained mass. An inner ball gives a positive radial lower bound proportional to ‖u‖, so the continuous hinge objective attains its minimum. Bounded difference quotients justify differentiating at nonzero u because the zero affine level is null. Near u=0 the hinge is inactive on all of compact K. Stationarity makes the first moment of the selected cap zero, so the hinge integral equals the cap volume. The pointwise inequality against any feasible f is sharp exactly for that cap's indicator a.e. A compact full-dimensional convex body is the closure of its interior, so two distinct such bodies cannot agree a.e. Off the centroid the cut has both signs in the interior, and equality of the cap determines its plane and the normal after normalization at the mark. At the centroid the whole body attains the volume bound.

Lower factor. The tangent to L^(−d−1) at L=1 is 1−(d+1)(L−1). Strict convexity gives strictness away from L=1 where the tangent is positive, and the inverse power remains positive where the clipped tangent is zero. With the attained nonzero energy parameter, L=1 is a null hyperplane. The zero energy parameter is optimal exactly at the ordinary centroid, where both optima equal |K|.

Height comparison in d≥2. Properness implies u_*≠0 and the height interval has a<0<b. The coarea factor is 1/‖u_*‖. Brunn–Minkowski applies to the parallel (d−1)-sections and yields concavity of the root on (a,b). The cap's mass and stationarity give exactly its mass T and mean height 1. Dilation about a point at height b gives height at least t at scale 1−t/b, and integration gives mean at least b/(d+1), so b≤B=d+1. The cone density on [0,B] integrates to T and has first moment TB/(d+1)=T.

Two matched moments. In the unequal case the positive set has positive length, and root concavity and the zero extension beyond b make it one interval up to endpoints. If it touches 0 or B, multiplication by the affine function vanishing at the other endpoint makes the signed density difference have one fixed sign and nonzero integral, contradicting the matched moments. Continuity at 0 and concavity along the segment from negative height to a positive height in the positive interval give a negative root difference at each interior negative height. In the equal case positivity of the comparison density forces b=B, continuity gives zero root difference on (0,B), and the same concavity gives a nonpositive difference to the left. The argument uses no continuity at the upper support endpoint. Subtracting the convex kernel's secant gives a nonpositive product with the density difference on each sign interval, and the affine term vanishes upon integration.

Strict upper factor. The test parameter −u_*/B has denominator (B+1−s)/B≥1/B on K. The positive convex kernel w has strict integrated comparison because the comparison density is positive at every height below a, while the actual density vanishes there. Substituting t=B−s and then r=t/(1+t) makes the cone integral (dT/B^d)∫_0^1 r^(d−1)dr=T/B^d. Multiplication by B^(d+1) gives E<BT. At the centroid E=T>0 also gives strictness.

Simplex and dimension one. Positive vertex values give precisely the admissible affine denominators when their λ-weighted sum is one. Positive rescaling of convex weights maps onto the image simplex. The augmented determinant gives image volume V/∏L_i, with each column multiplied by L_i and the last row restored by subtracting the affine denominator's linear part. Maximizing the product by AM–GM gives λ_iL_i=1/(d+1). In an interval the greatest centroidal subinterval is centered and has length 2min(ℓ,r). Barycentric weights r/(ℓ+r) and ℓ/(ℓ+r) give E=4ℓr/(ℓ+r), whose ratio to T is strictly below 2 for ℓ,r>0. Independently integrating the energy at a=1/3 on [−1,3] gives E=3 and T=2.

Sharpness and endpoints. For 0<ε≤1/(d+1) the hinge has value 1 at y and selects the dilation (d+1)ε K, whose centroid is y. The indicator attains the hinge bound even when the dilation fills K. Thus T=V(d+1)^dε^d and E=V(d+1)^(d+1)(1−dε)ε^d. Exact substitutions at (d,ε)=(1,1/4),(2,1/6),(3,1/8) give (T,E)=(1/2,3/4),(1/8,1/4),(1/48,5/96). The ratio is 1 at the centroid endpoint and tends to d+1 as ε decreases to zero along interior marks of the same simplex. Every admissible pair has a strictly smaller ratio.

summary: The hinge gives the unique maximum-volume centroidal cap. The tangent inequality is strict off the centroid. The comparison of coarea densities gives the strict upper factor d+1, with strictness supplied by the comparison density below the body's finite height support. The exact simplex family approaches this factor in every dimension, and both accepted dependencies apply.
